handoff_constraints: Keep Workflow execution deterministic: the same input must close the same gate/evidence sequence without random, network, database, or LLM side effects in the replay/reference path.
Use the in-memory reference as a contract test for future durable engines and broker adapters, not as a production Workflow runtime.
Separate execution-reference evidence from broker/event emission evidence so cloud readiness cannot imply a durable queue, child-service call, or audit-chain runtime.
Preserve vendor-neutral workflow handoff vocabulary so later Serverless Workflow/Temporal-style adapters can map the same gates without rewriting domain/app envelopes.

findings: Package, capability, execution status, changeset, and evidence names follow the enterprise-suite workflow-adapter naming pattern.
Root operating contract, Enterprise Suite spec, task ledger, multispectrum evidence, and audit-chain conventions are preserved.
The existing flat crates/ workflow adapter is extended in place and cloud-readiness composes it through a workspace path dependency.

The slice keeps Workflow execution reference logic in the in-memory adapter and keeps cloud-readiness as a control-plane composer; architecture-boundaries is expected to include one new workspace edge.
No external dependency is introduced; cloud-readiness adds one workspace path dependency on the existing workflow adapter.
Enterprise Suite JSON, catalog row, data_class annotations, and multispectrum evidence keep machine-readable shapes.

Execution is deterministic and bounded: it requires an existing dispatch, refuses duplicate execution, checks gate/evidence count drift, records each gate once, and sets all real runtime/cloud capability flags false.
The implementation is a small state-machine extension over the existing BTreeMap-backed queue; it adds no threads, no async runtime, no network call, and no broker.
A deterministic execution reference is now available for later Workflow-engine/broker/cloud adapters while production blockers remain explicit in cloud-readiness.
Tests cover execution without dispatch, duplicate execution, and gate/evidence drift to prevent false execution-readiness claims.
Future durable adapters get a concrete execution record shape with dispatch idempotency, execution idempotency, gate records, and explicit nonclaim flags.
The code keeps unsafe forbidden, uses typed statuses/errors, bounded vectors from validated envelopes, and no new third-party crates.

Alternatives considered: keep metadata-only dispatch, attach a real Workflow engine/broker now, or add a deterministic in-memory execution reference. The reference was selected because it is testable now and avoids runtime/cloud overclaims.
The execution reference stays behind the workflow dispatch port and cloud-readiness consumes only capability flags, preserving adapter/control-plane boundaries.
No child-service call, broker publish, credential handling, durable queue, or runtime audit emission is introduced; idempotency keys retain existing whitespace/path traversal refusal.
Execution is O(number of required gates) over an already prepared in-memory envelope and is outside any deployed request path.
Workflow adapter and cloud-readiness tests cover positive execution, local readiness composition, and negative overclaim/drift cases.

The slice strengthens evidence traceability for deterministic gate closure while keeping statutory filing, disbursement, production SLO, durable Workflow engine, and runtime audit-chain evidence as blockers.
Enterprise Suite spec, tasks, catalog data classes, evidence, and audit-chain rows document the execution reference and nonclaims.
The slice is additive and can be reverted by removing execution records/capability fields, cloud-readiness composition fields, and spec/task/evidence rows.
Execution records include gate evidence refs and status, but no runtime telemetry, audit-chain emission, or broker event is claimed.
Reserved facet not applicable; no special reserved-surface claim is made.
No data/schema migration is performed; durable Workflow engine, broker, cloud deployment, and runtime audit emission remain future migrations.

summary: Adds deterministic in-memory Enterprise Suite Workflow execution records and composes the capability into cloud-readiness without claiming durable Workflow engine or broker runtime.
